selection: Three small engineering tasks for technical screening, not representative of general development.

incremental-observation.origin: New incremental-observation requirements applied to the existing bridge/observation.mjs from repository commit 5e4bc6e. Component integration pilot, not a full application delivery.
incremental-observation.task:
Node.js 24, ESM, no third-party packages required. You may add focused tests and use ordinary file/shell tools. Preserve the stated interfaces. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and your additional checks. Do not change visible.test.mjs. Final acceptance will also exercise the specified edge cases. Do not inspect outside this workspace.
Update observation.mjs, which is the project's existing response-summary module. Keep detail='full' behavior and current essential fields unchanged. In summary mode, recentToolFailures must contain only failure events with seq greater than afterCursor (all failures when no cursor); omit that property when none are new. Add failureSeen=true when any supplied tool event failed, even if already reported. Add failureCoverage='partial' when toolEventsOmitted>0, otherwise 'complete'; do not claim omitted history was checked. Preserve pending approvals/questions and terminal state on unchanged observations. afterCursor, when supplied, must be a nonnegative safe integer, not greater than full.cursor; otherwise throw RangeError in summary mode. Validate full.cursor as a nonnegative safe integer in summary mode too. Summary must not mutate the supplied object or arrays. Existing latest-message behavior remains: at most 600 characters, explicit truncation flag, no repeated old message. Cover these requirements with focused tests.

usage-ledger.origin: New reusable accounting component needed by the DSH-led prototype; requirements authored before model runs. Engineering pilot, not a historical production bug.
usage-ledger.task:
Node.js 24, ESM, no third-party packages required. You may add focused tests and use ordinary file/shell tools. Preserve the stated interfaces. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and your additional checks. Do not change visible.test.mjs. Final acceptance will also exercise the specified edge cases. Do not inspect outside this workspace.
Implement usage-ledger.mjs exporting createLedger(), ingest(state,event), report(state,rates). State must survive JSON.stringify/parse and ingest mutates it in place. An event has id (globally unique nonempty string), stream (nonempty string identifying ONE model/provider/session), model (nonempty string), seq (nonnegative safe integer), kind ('delta' or 'cumulative'), input (inclusive of cached input), cachedInput, output (all nonnegative safe integers; cachedInput<=input). All usage fields required; unknown is not zero. A stream keeps one model and kind. Exact replays of an id must be no-ops even after restart; conflicting reuse throws without changing state. Reject out-of-order or repeated seq with a new id. Cumulative counters must never decrease individually; count only latest cumulative totals, rather than summing snapshots. Delta events sum. Validate safe-integer arithmetic and guarantee atomic ingestion: every rejection leaves state byte-for-byte unchanged. createLedger produces empty state. report returns {complete,totalUsd,byModel}; byModel[model] contains {uncachedInput,cacheRead,output}. rates[model] has uncachedInput,cacheRead,output USD per million, each finite and nonnegative. Sum all streams of the same model. Missing/invalid rates for an actually used model produce complete:false,totalUsd:null while preserving token totals. Empty ledger reports complete:true,totalUsd:0,byModel:{}. Do not round internal cost.

budget-reservations.origin: New crash-aware budget component needed before automated paid expert calls; requirements authored before runs. State machine pilot, not a full production deployment.
budget-reservations.task:
Node.js 24, ESM, no third-party packages required. You may add focused tests and use ordinary file/shell tools. Preserve the stated interfaces. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and your additional checks. Do not change visible.test.mjs. Final acceptance will also exercise the specified edge cases. Do not inspect outside this workspace.
Implement budget.mjs exporting createBudget(limit), reserve(state,id,amount), settle(state,id,actual), release(state,id), snapshot(state). All amounts are integer micro-dollars (safe nonnegative integers); id is a nonempty string. Functions mutate a JSON-serializable state. snapshot returns {limit,spent,reserved,available,overdrawn}. Reserve holds a maximum estimate before a remote call; active holds reduce available. A repeated reserve with same id+amount is an idempotent replay regardless of whether later settled/released; changed amount or reuse for a different operation throws. A new reserve exceeding available throws. settle records actual spend, frees its hold, and is idempotent only for exactly the same actual amount; actual may exceed the reservation and even total limit because remote charges cannot be undone: record the full actual spend, set available=max(0,limit-spent-reserved), and overdrawn=true iff spent+reserved>limit. Later new reservations cannot spend overdrawn budgets. release is only for a remote call known not to have run, frees an active hold, and repeats idempotently; it rejects an already settled id. settle rejects a released or unknown id. Never infer release from a timeout; an unresolved reservation survives JSON serialization and continues blocking spend after restart. Reject invalid input or unsafe arithmetic without changing state. Snapshot must not expose mutable internals. No filesystem or network needed in this module.
